1. The device running this app must act as the USB host (OTG). Check that it supports OTG and enable it in settings if a switch is available. Connect an OTG adapter to this device if needed.
2. Use a working data cable: a charge-only cable will not work. Try another cable and connect without a hub or extension cable.

3. On the TV or box, use the port intended for connection to a computer (ADB/USB device). A regular USB port for flash drives may not support this role. Check the model’s manual for the correct port and cable.
4. Enable USB debugging in Developer options on the target device. Unlock the screens, allow this app to access USB, and accept the debugging prompt on the target device.
5. Reconnect the cable and tap “Refresh USB devices”. If that does not help, restart the devices. If no debugging prompt appears, revoke USB debugging authorizations on the target and reconnect.
If you cannot connect for USB debugging through the mobile app, try the desktop app for Windows, Linux, or macOS and connect the target device to your computer.

The reference contains commands supported by the embedded client and Android shell examples. Shell commands depend on the firmware: query them using Device command help. Each command uses a new non-interactive shell on the selected device. Pipes, quotes and scripts work there; cd does not carry over. No interactive stdin or binary output in the console. Commands stop after 5 minutes. Use logcat -d or top -b -n 1 for snapshots. The app implements shell, file transfer, APK installation and device services; desktop ADB server options, forward/reverse, fastboot and sideload file flashing are not implemented. devices lists only the connection selected in this app; disconnect closes that connection, including USB. File transfer supports individual files without compression. Installation supports -r, -t, -d, -g, --user, --abi, -i, --instant, --full, --dont-kill and --streaming.
These are files added from this phone or received from the connected device. Adding a file does not send or install it. Choose an install or send command, review it in the console, then press Run.

Commands run on the selected connected device and can change system settings, install or remove apps, and erase data. An incorrect command may disrupt the device or cause data loss. Check the target device and only run commands whose effects you understand.
Auto-scroll follows new output. Turn it off to read earlier lines.

Add files from this device opens the system document picker and copies the selected documents or APKs into this list.

APK install command fills the console with adb install. Run installs the app on the connected device.

Send file command fills the console with adb push. The default destination is /sdcard/Download on the connected device; edit the path before running if needed.

Insert name into command appends the selected file name to the current input without running anything.

Download from connected device asks for the full remote file path and starts the download after confirmation. The received file appears here.

Save to this device opens the system save dialog and saves a copy from this list to your phone. It does not access the connected device.
Enter the full path of a file on the connected device. Download copies it into Files and APK. Then use Save to this device to choose a folder on your phone.
